subject: Post-demo: Stress-window & SLO handoff for burst readiness
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Elena Morales <elena@nimbushealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, sergio_alvarez@redwood.com
Date: 2026-09-15T14:03:00-07:00
Subject: Post-demo: Stress-window & SLO handoff for burst readiness

Hi Elena — thanks again for taking the demo today. Quick recap and proposed next steps focused on the performance/SLO items we discussed so your engineering team can validate internal constraints before a pilot.

Key SLOs you mentioned on the call:
- P95 tail latency for streaming completions <= 300ms (goal) / <= 400ms (acceptable)
- Sustained steady-state throughput target: 120 req/s per model variant
- Concurrency target: 250 concurrent streaming sessions
- Burst readiness: handle up to 1,200 requests/sec for short windows (30–90s) with graceful degradation beyond that

What we covered re: autoscale and warm pools:
- Warm pool recommendation: maintain 8–12 pre-warmed worker slots for the primary model in your us-east region during business hours; this keeps cold-starts to a minimum for expected burst windows.
- Scale-up times: cold scaling (spin up new worker on Dedicated) we measured at ~45–75s depending on GPU type; warm pool transitions are sub-2s for request routing once a slot is reserved.
- Queueing behavior: we propose a bounded soft-queue (max 500ms enqueue) with priority routing for authenticated enterprise tokens to avoid head-of-line blocking.

Attachments: demo slides and a sample stress request payload (nimbus-stress-sample-requests.json) for your perf team to run.

Next steps (suggested):
1) Your engineering team runs the attached stress payload against a shorttrial Redwood sandbox config (we can spin this up tomorrow).
2) Marissa to send the exact warm-pool configuration and an infra checklist for the trial.
3) We hold a follow-up tech sync for telemetry mapping (latency buckets, token rates) — propose Thu 9/17 10am ET.

If any of the SLO numbers above should be different, flag them and we’ll adjust the trial parameters.

Thanks,
Karthik
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
---
Attachments: 20260915-demo-slides.pdf, nimbus-stress-sample-requests.json
From: Elena Morales <elena@nimbushealth.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: platform@NimbusHealth.com, procure@nimbushealth.com
Date: 2026-09-15T16:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Stress-window & SLO handoff for burst readiness

Thanks Karthik — great demo. A few clarifications from our side after reviewing with platform: 

1) Latency needs to be stricter for our triage workflow. We need P95 <= 250ms for short messages (under 512 tokens). Can you confirm whether that is realistic with your streaming path and our model choice?
2) Burst profile: the 1,200 rps window is correct for peak alerts. Typically bursts last 45–60s, but we have occasional multi-minute surges (120–180s) when a partner system retries.
3) Warm pool sizing: 8–12 sounds reasonable; would like to see cost delta between warm pool of 8 vs. 16.

We’ll run the sample payload but please have the trial config include token-level tracing and per-request trace_id so our telemetry team can map traces back to our system.

Elena
Director of Platform Engineering | Nimbus Health
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Elena Morales <elena@nimbushealth.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: sergio_alvarez@redwood.com
Date: 2026-09-15T18:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Stress-window & SLO handoff for burst readiness

Elena — quick technical follow-up from our SRE/solutions perspective. Peter (SRE) asked that I capture the measured numbers we can provide in the trial: 

- Streaming P95 observed (internal Redwood benchmark, similar model family, 512 tokens): 220–260ms with warm pool active and small-batch continuous batching enabled.
- Cold start delta (no warm slot): adds ~650–900ms on first request for a new worker on the GPU profile you saw.
- Warm-pool transition: once slot is warm, routing to slot is <100ms; the sub-2s number Karthik referenced is for worker reservation time when spin-up is needed.
- Throughput: single worker (A100-equivalent) handles ~160 streaming sessions concurrent with sustained per-session throughput; aggregate throughput scales linearly with warm slot count until you hit kernel contention (rare at your target).

Queueing proposals:
- Soft-queue max latency: 500ms (configurable). We can also expose a policy to drop requests or apply a token-cost-based prioritization when queue depth exceeds threshold.

I’ll attach a short YAML snippet in the trial config describing warm_pool.min = 8, warm_pool.max = 16, scale.policy.burst_window_secs = 120, and scale.policy.target_rps = 120.

Marissa
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Date: 2026-09-16T08:05:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: trial config & cost estimate for Elena

Karthik — drafting the quick cost delta for warm pool sizes. Notes for the proposal to Elena: 

- Warm pool of 8 (A100-equivalent slots) estimated incremental monthly cost: ~$9.6k (on Dedicated pricing assumptions)
- Warm pool of 16 estimated incremental monthly cost: ~$18.1k
- For a pilot (2 week trial) pro-rated: 8-slot ~= $4.4k; 16-slot ~= $8.3k. Recommend we offer a 50% pilot credit to shorten procurement friction.

Operational notes:
- Suggest enabling per-request preemption for higher SLA tokens so we preserve P95 for triage traffic during burst events.
- Add an alert if scaled capacity takes longer than 90s to reach target capacity — we can use this as a trigger for Canary rollback or fallback to smaller model variant.

Grace — adding you so leadership is aware we plan to offer a pilot credit and want approval to proceed.

Sergio
Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: Elena Morales <elena@nimbushealth.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, sergio_alvarez@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: procure@nimbushealth.com
Date: 2026-09-16T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Stress-window & SLO handoff for burst readiness

Appreciate the fast turnaround — this looks good. A couple quick confirmations before we kick off the pilot: 

- We confirm P95 <= 250ms hard requirement for short messages; please include that as a pass/fail criterion in the trial report.
- Please include token-level tracing and trace_id mapping in the trial outputs. Without those we can’t correlate to our upstream retries.
- We accept a 2-week trial with a 50% pilot credit; procurement will send the short MSA next week.

I’ll have our platform team run the attached load profile tomorrow and share results by EOD Friday. If anything changes on our side we’ll flag it early.

Thanks all — looking forward to the tech sync on Thu.

Elena
Director of Platform Engineering | Nimbus Health
